doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Double bass drums and the great drummers
title: The drummers' fraternity
summary: Drummers covered for one another on dates and went to hear each other, and Buddy Rich was forever taking his hi-hat and snare.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: It sounds like the drummers was a fraternity of sorts. It sounds like you guys had a real rapport and looked out for one another? Is that really the case?

Oh yeah, yes, absolutely. To the extent, if one guy couldn’t make – like if I was out in California working for Quincy Jones and I couldn’t make a certain date, I’d call Shelly Manne or Earl Palmer or Paul Humphrey. We’d always look out for one another. Drummers were very close, and we would go hear one another, like Buddy Rich coming to hear me play. I’d go hear him play. One thing about him: he always used to cop my hi- hat and my snare drum. I’d come to the gig at night, and no snare drum and hi-hat. Good thing I had an extra. I said, that darn Buddy Rich – took my hi-hat and my snare drum.
